title: Sir Henry Clinton Papers (British Headquarters Papers)
issues: URL https://quod.lib.umich.edu/c/clementsmss/umich-wcl-M-1 is blocked by a Cloudflare JavaScript challenge, preventing direct verification of the content at this specific path.

The parenthetical '(British Headquarters Papers)' conflates two distinct archival collections: the Sir Henry Clinton Papers at the William L. Clements Library (University of Michigan) and the British Headquarters Papers (Carleton/Dorchester Papers, PRO 30/55) held at The National Archives (UK). These are separate collections. The Clinton Papers contain British HQ correspondence but are not formally titled 'British Headquarters Papers.'
Institution listed as 'William L. Clements Library, University of Michigan' is correct for the Clinton Papers specifically, but the combined title creates ambiguity.
recommendation: Clarify whether the citation refers to the Sir Henry Clinton Papers (Clements Library) or the British Headquarters Papers (UK National Archives). Remove the conflating parenthetical or disambiguate with two separate citations. Confirm the specific Clements finding aid URL once accessible.

title: Letters of Delegates to Congress, 1774-1789 (26 vols.)
issues: URL https://memory.loc.gov/ammem/amlaw/lwdg.html redirects (HTTP 301) to an article/essay page describing the Letters of Delegates collection, not to the digitized letters themselves.

The 'Letters of Delegates to Congress' (26 volumes, edited by Paul H. Smith et al., published 1976-2000) is a modern scholarly edition — an editorially compiled, transcribed, and annotated collection assembled from dozens of repositories. As a published edited compilation, it is a secondary source by nature. The underlying individual letters are primary, but this citation points to the compiled edition, not original manuscripts.
Labeling an edited twentieth-century scholarly compilation as TIER1 primary overstates its evidential standing compared to the original holograph letters.
recommendation: Reclassify as TIER2 (secondary/edited primary) or replace with citations to specific original letters at their holding institutions. If using LOC's digitized version, link directly to the collection's browsable interface rather than the essay redirect.
